transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-26 16:00 UTC | Duration: 42m
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Mark Rivera (Horizon - Head of ML), Sophie Chen (Horizon - Platform Eng), Lars Olsen (Horizon - FinOps)

00:00 Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
00:05 Mark Rivera: Yep, loud and clear. Sorry, just finishing something, good to go.
00:18 Alex: Cool. Quick agenda — Priya will walk through the Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards and then we'll show cost breakdowns and some Optimize recommendations. We'll leave time for security and pilot questions. Sound good?
00:30 Sophie Chen: Sounds good. We're mainly interested in per-route cost, like which paths are burning tokens in prod.
00:40 Priya Desai: Great, I'll jump in — sharing my screen now. Let me know if the view is fuzzy, sometimes the screen share compresses.
00:55 Priya: Alright, this is the Console home, you'll see the overview — total tokens, latency percentiles, error rates. You'll notice we automatically map traffic to routes so you can filter by model, route, and environment.
01:20 Lars Olsen: When you say route, is that our API route or per-feature? We have multiple frontend features hitting the same endpoint currently.
01:35 Priya: Good question — route is the logical endpoint as defined in your integration. You can also tag requests server-side so we can split by feature. Many customers use route tags to separate chat, search, summarization etc.
01:50 Mark: Ok. Show the cost view.
02:00 Priya: Yep — switching to cost analytics. Here is per-route cost over time, and we break down by model, tokens, embeddings, and other units. You can set a cost window and compare week over week.
02:25 Priya: You'll also see per-token unit price estimates based on your committed tier or host pricing. For Dedicated we plug in reserved rates. For hosted we use usage rates.
02:40 Sophie: How accurate are the unit price estimates? We run lots of short prompts, a lot of small requests — the aggregation sometimes hides tail effects.
02:55 Priya: The Console uses exact token accounting from the runtime, but we do round-trip adjustments for streaming and partial responses. For very small requests the per-request overhead can change effective cost — we surface both token-only and full-request cost so you can see that distinction.
03:20 Alex: Also, Optimize suggests batching/caching profiles per route which we can apply to reduce per-token costs without hurting latency for most routes.
03:35 Mark: Show how those suggestions look.
03:40 Priya: Sure — here's an example route. We analyze sequence length distribution, average latency, and KV cache hit rates. Then we recommend a batching window and whether prefix caching would help. See, it estimates 18% cost reduction if you enable prefix caching plus batching of 50ms for this route.
04:10 Lars: Does that change latency? 50ms batching sounds like it could add tail latency spikes.
04:20 Priya: We simulate latency SLOs — the recommendation includes an expected p95 impact. For many conversational routes p50 is unchanged and p95 increases by ~10ms; we let you pick cost vs latency targets. You can also set automatic fallbacks to route to lower-cost model variants if SLOs are violated.
04:50 Sophie: What about quantization recommendations? We have a mix of Llama and Mistral variants in our map.
05:00 Priya: We run model-compat checks and recommend quantization profiles that maintain quality per your evals. Console surfaces expected quality impact and estimated token cost savings.
05:20 Mark: Can we see a per-user or per-team breakdown? Our product teams want to understand spend by feature owner.
05:30 Priya: Yes — we have per- route + tag breakdowns. You can create dashboards and grant RBAC scoping so product teams only see their routes.
05:50 Alex: On the security side we integrate with SSO/SAML, audit logs, and KMS for key management — happy to share the SOC2 pack.
06:05 Sophie: Please do. Also need VPC/on-prem info for our regulated clients.
06:15 Alex: We'll include the Private deployment whitepaper and the network topology doc.
06:25 Mark: Back to cost — can you export a CSV with per-route token counts and cost estimates so our FinOps can ingest?
06:35 Priya: Yep exportable CSV and an API endpoint to pull the same metrics. We also have a streaming telemetry hook for SIEM.
06:48 Lars: One thing — how do you attribute shared prompts? We have a single chat model used by multiple features. Attribution is tricky.
07:00 Priya: We recommend an enforced header/tag from the application layer; otherwise we do heuristic attribution by route and prompt signature. It's best to tag at ingestion.
07:20 Mark: Let's drill into the cost breakdown UI.
07:25 Priya: Ok — here you see cost waterfall per route: model price, token counts, batching adjustments, caching savings, and overhead like network/egress if Private. The UI shows both raw token cost and amortized cost after batching/caching.
07:50 Sophie: Can we run a what-if? Eg, if we change to a quantized model or enable 100ms batching what happens to spend and latency?
08:05 Priya: Yes — there's a scenarios panel. You can toggle quantization, batching windows, or model variants and it will recalc expected cost and latency. We also show confidence intervals based on traffic variance.
08:30 Mark: Nice. For pilot scope we want to focus on 3 routes: product-search, support-chat, order-summarize. Can we restrict the pilot to those?
08:44 Alex: Absolutely, pilots are commonly scoped to a set of routes. We can provision a dedicated tenant or run them on hosted with strict tagging.
09:00 Lars: Cost allocation — can we push cost back into our chargeback system?
09:10 Priya: You can export per-route cost CSVs or call the metrics API to feed your internal chargeback. We also have a usage webhook for near real-time reporting.
09:25 Mark: Anything about billing smoothing? Our finance team wants to avoid big variance month-to-month.
09:35 Alex: We offer reserved capacity for Dedicated as committed throughput which smooths unit cost, plus governance via quotas and alerts. We'll outline options in pricing doc.
09:50 Sophie: Show alerts — we want to get notified if cost per route spikes or if cache hit rate drops.
10:02 Priya: Alerts live in the Console — you can set metric thresholds (cost per minute, token/sec, cache hit %). Alerts can go to Slack, PagerDuty, or email. They include a link to the route and a snapshot of the last hour.
10:28 Mark: Is there correlation with quality regressions? We once rolled a quantized model and saw hallucination regressions. Can we tie evals to cost changes?
10:42 Priya: Yes — Console integrates with our Eval harness. You can attach prompt sets to a route and get quality metrics side-by-side with cost. We also do regression alerts when quality drops beyond a threshold after a rollout.
11:05 Sophie: How does fallback work for rollouts?
11:12 Priya: Rollouts can be canary, A/B, or percent-based. If a rollout violates latency or quality thresholds we auto- revert or route traffic to the previous variant.
11:28 Lars: For the pilot, we need SOC2 docs and encryption details up front.
11:35 Alex: We'll send SOC2 and the SAML/KMS integration guide in the follow-up bundle.
11:45 Mark: Regarding data residency — some of our EU customers require data never leave EU. How does Private handle that?
11:55 Priya: Private provides a control plane in your VPC or on-prem. For hosted we offer region pinning and data residency controls; for strict regulations we recommend a Private deployment. We'll include region topology in the docs.
12:18 Sophie: Ok, demo the per-route drilldown for product-search please.
12:22 Priya: Drilling in now — here's request distribution, prompt length histogram, p50/p95 latency, token spend, and the Optimize suggestions on the right. You can expand the suggestion to see expected savings and a short rationale.
12:50 Mark: The histogram looks skewed — many very short prompts and a tail of long ones. That could be an opportunity for prefix caching on the long ones.
13:05 Priya: Exactly, prefix caching helps for repeated prefixes; we also recommend re-structuring prompts and using shorter system prompts where possible.
13:20 Lars: Any limits on the number of custom dashboards? Our teams like dozens.
13:30 Alex: No hard limits, just plan for retention — dashboards can query long retention windows if you have the add-on for extended observability.
13:45 Sophie: How granular is RBAC? We need to ensure only FinOps sees cost data and engineers don't see customer PII.
13:55 Priya: RBAC is role-based with attribute filters; you can mask fields and enforce least privilege. Audit logs capture who viewed what.
14:12 Mark: Ok, show me the export sample for product-search.
14:16 Priya: Exporting now — you'll get CSV with timestamp, route, token_in, token_out, model, estimated_cost, tags. Here's a quick sample link I'm pasting in chat.
14:30 Sophie: We saw earlier a 18% estimate from batching + caching, how confident are those numbers?
14:40 Priya: The system uses historical traffic and simulates the change. Confidence depends on variance — we show a confidence band. For low variance routes confidence is higher. That's why we ask for sample traffic logs for pilot benchmarking.
14:58 Alex: If you want we can run an internal benchmark on your sample and return a pilot plan with expected savings and a recommended deployment (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).
15:10 Mark: That'd be perfect. Timeline? We want results before end of April.
15:20 Alex: We can do a 2-week pilot: handoff + instrumentation week, 1-week benchmark, then results. Kickoff the week of Apr 5 should work.
15:40 Lars: Are there any tricky edge cases you usually see?
15:45 Priya: Yeah, untagged traffic, mixing many model variants without eval alignment, and chat systems where user messages are large — those require prompt engineering and careful caching.
16:00 Sophie: About pricing: can you show a simple hosted vs reserved example?
16:10 Alex: Sure — hosted is pure usage; reserved gives lower unit cost for committed throughput. I'll send a tailored sheet showing your estimated monthly tokens and cost at both tiers.
16:30 Mark: One last question — for Dedicated, how do you handle autoscaling and burst capacity? We have seasonal spikes.
16:40 Priya: Dedicated supports autoscaling policies and burst pools. You can configure a baseline reserved capacity and set burst to handle spikes with a fallback policy to hosted if capacity is exhausted.
16:55 Sophie: Great. Let's recap real quick.
17:00 Alex: Recap: Alex will send pricing and security docs; Priya will share recording and dashboards; Mark will provide sample traffic and route list for pilot; plan to kickoff the week of 2026-04-05.
17:18 Mark: Sounds good, thanks both.
17:25 Alex: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in Slack and email with the bundle.
17:30 End of call.
